newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Sale of 6 Russia oil firm stakes set July 1-Oct 21.
newsitem.headline: Sale of 6 Russia oil firm stakes set July 1-Oct 21.

text.p: Auctions of state stakes in six Russian energy companies will open on separate dates between July 1 and October 21, the Federal Property Fund said on Monday.

It said auctions of government shares in KomiTEK and the East-Siberian Oil and Gas Company would begin on July 1. Sales of shares in the Tyumen Oil Company would begin on August 5, the Eastern Oil Company on August 26, Norsi-Oil on October 7 and the Siberian-Urals Oil Company (SIBUR) on October 21. The fund said the auctions carried no restrictions, meaning foreigners could make bids for some of the shares.

The sales are part of Moscow's drive to raise up to $1 billion fast for the budget and reflect the aggressive privatisation of the vital oil sector. Russia is the world's third largest crude oil producer.

The fund said 48.68 percent of the charter capital of the Tyumen Oil Company would be offered, each share nominally worth five roubles. The auction will be open to bids until September 26 and the winner would be named by October 24.

It said 51 percent of the charter capital of the Eastern Oil Company would be offered, each share with a face value of two roubles. Bids may be placed until October 31, and the winner of the auction would be chosen by December 1.

The Norsi-Oil stake would represent 45.45 percent of the charter capital. Each share has a face value of 2.5 roubles. The auction would remain open until December 5, with the winner chosen no later than December 29.

The fund said 36.28 percent of SIBUR's charter capital would be up for sale. Each share has a nominal value of eight roubles. Bids would be accepted until December 5, and the winner would be named no later than December 29. The fund said starting prices had yet to be decided.
It announced earlier on Monday that auctions for state stakes in KomiTEK and the East-Siberian Oil and Gas Company would open July 1.
